Most of our back end is written in C Sharp on .net 8 and the front end uses React with Typescript. We deploy everything to Azure. And we use SQL server for the main database and Redis for caching. So my first question is a simple one. Can you tell me about yourself and about your last project? Take your time, there is no rush at all. I see that sounds interesting. III think I would like to hear a bit more about the architecture of that project. How did you? Split the system into services and how did those services talk to each other? Did you use a message queue or did the services call each other directly over HTTP? And how did you handle failures? For example when one service was slow or completely down? Good. Now let me ask you something more technical. What is dependency injection in C sharp and why is it useful? Can you explain the difference between a transient, a scoped and a Singleton lifetime? When would you choose each one? And what can go wrong if you choose the wrong lifetime? For example, what happens if a Singleton service depends on a scope database context? Let me repeat that question because it is important. What happens if a Singleton service depends on a scope database context OK? Let us move on to databases. Imagine a table with 42 million rows of bookings. A query that searches bookings by customer and by date has become very slow during the last month. How would you find out why it is slow and what would you do to make it fast again? Would you add an index and if so which columns would you put in it and in which order? What are the costs of adding too many indexes to a table that receives a lot of rights? Now a question about async code. What is the difference between a task and a thread? Why is it a bad idea to call result or wait on a task inside an Asp.net request? Have you ever seen a deadlock caused by async code and how did you fix it? Next I would like to talk about testing. How do you decide what to cover with unit tests and what to cover with integration tests? Do you write the tests before the code, after the code, or does it depend on the situation? Tell me about a bug that reached production. Even though you had tests, what did you learn from it? Let us talk about teamwork for a minute.
